keyDecisions.decision: Close is a method on Closer{Layout, Repository}, taking a ShippedByHand{Order, URL, Approver} parameter object, not a flat function
keyDecisions.reasoning: A flat function would need 7 parameters (ledger, orders, layout, repo, id, url, approver), over the project's 4-parameter hard limit; bundling the two structural dependencies into a receiver and the three call-specific values into one parameter object keeps Close itself at 3 parameters.

keyDecisions.decision: Extracted archiveAndRemove(order, layout, repo) string out of Supervisor.ship, and have both ship and Close call it
keyDecisions.reasoning: Close needed the exact same archive-then-remove sequence and warning wording ship already has; extracting once avoids duplicating that control flow and its two error-message templates (Kent Beck's no-duplication rule, Boy Scout Rule since finish.go was already being touched).

keyDecisions.decision: closeable only ever permits PhaseParked or PhaseStopped; every other phase, including PhaseShipped, is refused with RequestRerun's existing wording, duplicated as a literal rather than shared
keyDecisions.reasoning: Matches the acceptance criteria's refusal list exactly (running, retrying, waiting, completed, committed, pushed, proposed, already shipped) with one allow-list check; the wording is duplicated rather than extracted into a shared helper because the match is an AC requirement for two call sites, not a generalizable abstraction, and touching RequestRerun would mix an unrelated refactor into this diff.

keyDecisions.decision: isHTTPURL uses only net/url.Parse — true iff scheme is http or https and Host is non-empty, with zero network I/O
keyDecisions.reasoning: Structurally guarantees the 'close never fetches the URL' requirement: there is no code path to a network call because isHTTPURL imports nothing that could make one.

keyDecisions.decision: entryUpdates[EventShipped] folds a non-empty Entry.URL onto OrderState.URL; ApprovedBy is left in the ledger entry only, not folded onto OrderState
keyDecisions.reasoning: status only needs to display the URL; the approver's provenance belongs in the ledger (the audit record), not duplicated onto the in-memory projection. The non-empty guard makes this a no-op for every EventShipped line the supervisor's own ship() already writes, so no existing behavior changes.

notesForQa: Golden path and every refusal path from the acceptance criteria are covered by tests in internal/factory/control_test.go (unit level, using the existing testFactory fixture with a real git worktree) and cmd/loom/cmd/factory_inprocess_test.go (CLI level, using writeLedger to stand up orders in each disallowed phase).
